Retrieve the test results recording what each means produced when it was exercised.

Analysis:
Trace sampled obligations back to the law, regulation or contract cited to confirm the duty and its timescale.
Identify obligations left with no mechanism or no owning team and confirm each sits on the gap list with a date.
Compare the change log against legal changes and new processing in the period to find obligations that should have moved.
Set the test results beside the register to confirm each means delivered what is owed inside the stated timescale.
Review the remediation raised for each shortfall for a named owner and a closure date.

Output:
An assessment of register completeness against the legal and contractual sources cited.
A list of obligations with no discharging means or no owning team.
A table of exercised means with the outcome produced and the timescale met or missed.
A findings log of unrecorded register changes and open remediation.

title.en: Determine the obligations owed to PII principals and the law or contract behind each

description.en: Before any request arrives, work out what the organisation actually owes the people whose PII it holds: which privacy laws reach it, which contracts and published notices add commitments of their own, and what timescale each obligation carries. Obligations differ by jurisdiction and by relationship — an employee, a customer and a person whose PII arrived from a partner are rarely owed the same things — so a single undifferentiated list hides the gaps rather than closing them. Cite the source against every row, because an obligation nobody can trace back gets re-argued at the moment it has to be met. Attach the register with the obligation, its source and its timescale recorded per row.

evidenceHint.en: Obligations register listing each obligation owed to PII principals with the jurisdiction, the law or contract it comes from and the timescale it carries

text.en: List the jurisdictions the organisation's PII principals belong to.
Record the privacy law that binds the organisation in each of them.
Add the commitments made to principals in contracts and notices.
Write one register row per obligation, citing the source that creates it.
State the timescale each obligation must be met within.

title.en: Assign each registered obligation the means that discharges it, and open work where there is none

description.en: An obligation with nothing behind it is an intention. Go down the register and name, for each row, the concrete thing that discharges it — a form, an endpoint, a monitored inbox with a rota, a written procedure — and the team that runs it. The rows where the honest answer is that nothing does are the point of this task: they leave it as dated work with a named owner rather than as a register entry that reads as satisfied because it was written down. Attach the mapping together with the gap list.

evidenceHint.en: Obligation-to-means mapping naming the mechanism and the operating team behind each obligation, with a dated gap list for the obligations that have neither

text.en: Name the mechanism that discharges each registered obligation.
Record the system, channel or procedure the mechanism runs on.
Name the team that operates that means day to day.
Flag every obligation with no means standing behind it.
Raise each flagged gap as dated work with a named owner.

title.en: Log every change of law, contract or processing that moves an obligation in the register

description.en: The register is worth what its last update is worth, and obligations move for three reasons: the law changes, the organisation opens a new market or launches new processing, and contracts are signed or ended. Record each movement as it happens with the date and what prompted it, and note which means has to change as a result. An obligation that quietly acquires a shorter deadline is then met late by a process nobody was told to speed up, and the failure surfaces as a complaint rather than as a change. Attach the register change log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Register change log for the period giving each obligation added, altered or withdrawn, what prompted it, the date it was recorded and the means it affects

text.en: Record each legal or regulatory change that alters an obligation.
Add the obligations created by new processing or a new market.
Withdraw the rows whose obligation no longer applies, with the reason.
Note which means has to change and who was told to change it.
Date every entry so the register's currency can be read.

title.en: Exercise each means and compare what it produced against what is owed

description.en: Run the means rather than reading its description: walk the procedure, call the endpoint, read what actually reaches the person at the end of it. Compare the result against the obligation as the register states it, and against the timescale as well as the outcome, because a means that produces the right answer three weeks late has not discharged anything. Record each shortfall against the obligation it belongs to and route it to that obligation's owner with a remediation date. Attach the test results for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Test results per obligation recording what the means produced, whether it met the obligation inside its timescale, and the remediation raised for every shortfall

text.en: Select each obligation and run the means that discharges it.
Compare what came back against what the obligation requires.
Check the timescale was met, not only the outcome.
Record every obligation its means failed to discharge.
Route each shortfall to its owner with a remediation date.

templates.title: Downstream Notification of Corrections and Erasures
templates.description: Implements 7.3.7: when PII is corrected, erased or its processing restricted, every third party that already received that PII is told, so the change reaches the copies the organisation no longer holds.
templates.objective: To ensure a correction, erasure or restriction applied to PII reaches every third party already holding a copy, so the change takes effect beyond the organisation's own stores.
templates.successCriteria:
Each downstream holder of PII appears in the notification matrix with the change types it must be told of and the route that reaches it.
Corrections, erasures and restrictions raise the outbound notice without a manual prompt, and every dispatch is logged with its acknowledgement.
Exemptions from notifying a recipient carry the reason recorded against them.
Sampled changes leave no downstream copy still holding the superseded value.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the per-recipient notification matrix showing which of correction, erasure and restriction each downstream holder must be told of.
Collect the notice specification and the workflow wiring that raises a notice from each change type.
Acquire the downstream notification log for the period with dispatch dates and acknowledgements.
Gather the exemptions relied on and the reason recorded against each.
Retrieve the verification sample comparing changed records against what recipients confirm they hold.

Analysis:
Compare the matrix against the recipients named in transfer and disclosure records to find PII holders it omits.
Trace sampled corrections, erasures and restrictions from the source record to the notice raised, confirming the workflow fired unprompted.
Identify dispatches with no acknowledgement returned and measure how long they have stood open.
Test each claimed exemption against the ground recorded for it.
Follow every downstream copy still carrying the superseded value through to its correction.

Output:
A coverage assessment of the notification matrix against known PII recipients.
A trace of sampled changes from source record to dispatched notice and acknowledgement.
A list of unacknowledged notices and exemptions with no supporting ground.
A statement of downstream copies found out of date and how each was resolved.

title.en: Determine which parties already holding PII must be told of a later correction, erasure or restriction

description.en: This control starts where the change is already made in your own systems. For each party that was sent PII and still holds it, settle whether a later correction, a later erasure or a later restriction has to be passed on to them, and which of the three — the answer is rarely the same for all three or the same for every recipient. Record the route that can actually reach each one, and where notification would be impossible or out of proportion to the change, write that judgement and its reason down now, because the same judgement made on the day a request lands is the one nobody can defend afterwards.

evidenceHint.en: Per-recipient notification matrix giving, for each downstream holder, which of correction, erasure and restriction it must be told of, the route that reaches it, and every exemption with the reason recorded

text.en: Draw the recipient list for each PII category from the records already held.
Record for each whether corrections, erasures and restrictions must be passed on.
Name the contact or endpoint at each party that can receive such a notice.
Write down any recipient where notification is judged disproportionate, with the reason.

title.en: Build the outbound notice that carries a correction, erasure or restriction to each recipient

description.en: A notice is only useful if the recipient can act on it, so it has to name the record, say what changed or was erased, say which processing must now stop, and give the date the change took effect on your side. Build that notice and the route it travels — an API call, a ticket raised in the partner's own queue, a signed file drop, an email to the named contact where nothing better exists — and wire raising it into the correction, erasure and restriction workflows themselves. A change applied in your database while three recipients keep serving the old value is not finished, and the workflow that ends at your own write is what lets that happen.

evidenceHint.en: Notice specification plus the workflow wiring that raises it automatically from each correction, erasure and restriction, showing the acknowledgement path back from the recipient

text.en: Write the notice format naming the record, the change and the date applied.
Choose the sending route each recipient can actually receive and act on.
Connect the notice to the correction, erasure and restriction workflows.
Require an acknowledgement from the recipient that the change was applied.

title.en: Notify each recipient when PII they hold is corrected, erased or restricted, and log the dispatch

description.en: Work the notices as the changes happen rather than in a batch at period end, since a restriction that arrives late has already been ignored. For every correction, erasure or restriction applied, send the notice to each recipient the matrix names and record what went where and when. A recipient that never acknowledges is an open item, not a closed one — chase it and record the chase. Where no notice went out because an exemption applied, log that against the change too, so the silence reads as a decision someone took rather than a step somebody forgot.

evidenceHint.en: Downstream notification log for the period: the record changed, the recipients notified, the date sent, the acknowledgement received, and every exemption relied on

text.en: Send the notice to every recipient the matrix names for that record.
Record the date sent, the recipient and the change the notice carried.
Track each acknowledgement and chase the recipients that do not reply.
Log every case where the exemption was relied on instead of notifying.

title.en: Sample corrections and erasures from the period and verify the downstream copies changed too

description.en: Take a sample of the changes applied during the period and follow each one out to the parties that hold copies: ask what value they hold now, or for confirmation that the record is gone and the processing stopped. The log proves a notice was sent; only the recipient's answer proves it was applied, and the gap between the two is the whole point of this check. List every recipient still showing the superseded value, and count a recipient who cannot answer the question alongside those that answered wrongly.

evidenceHint.en: Verification sample comparing each corrected, erased or restricted record against what its recipients confirm they now hold, naming every downstream copy still out of date

text.en: Select a sample of the corrections, erasures and restrictions applied.
Check a notice was raised for each recipient the matrix names.
Ask the recipient to confirm the value it now holds or the deletion.
List the recipients still holding the superseded value or processing.

templates.title: Solely automated decision making
templates.description: Implements 7.3.10: decisions about a person that take effect with no human involvement are identified and disclosed as such, each one carries a route to a reviewer with authority to overturn it, and that review is checked for being more than a signature.
templates.objective: To ensure decisions taken about a person with no human involvement are known and disclosed as such, and that a contested one reaches a reviewer with authority to overturn it.
templates.successCriteria:
The decision inventory marks every decision that takes effect with no human review, the system producing it and its effect on the person.
Each such decision is disclosed as automated to the person it concerns and carries a route to a named reviewer.
The reviewer holds authority to change the outcome, and every intervention request is logged with what it produced.
Override rates show review altering outcomes rather than confirming them, and the inventory is re-checked after each rule or model change.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the decision inventory identifying decisions that take effect with no human review and the systems producing them.
Collect the walk-through of the live challenge path from decision notice to reviewer queue.
Acquire the automated decision log for the period with volumes per decision type and the rule set or model version in force.
Gather the intervention requests raised and the outcome recorded against each.
Retrieve the review-quality analysis reporting the override rate per decision type.

Analysis:
Follow sampled decision types through the processing chain to confirm the inventory marks those no person can alter before they take effect.
Trace a challenge along the live path and confirm it reaches the named reviewer rather than the team that produced the decision.
Confirm the reviewer's role carries authority to overturn the outcome, not only to record the objection.
Compare override rates across decision types and examine those where review has never changed an outcome.
Check that each rule set or model version change in the log triggered a re-check of the inventory.

Output:
A verified inventory of solely automated decisions with the effect of each on the individual.
A walk-through record of the challenge path with timings and the reviewer reached.
An override-rate table by decision type naming the types never challenged.
A finding list of decisions operating outside the inventory or with no challenge route.

title.en: Trace each decision about an individual to the point where a person can still change it

description.en: Take every decision the organisation reaches about a person — a price, a credit limit, a fraud hold, a refused application, a suspended account — and follow it forward to the last point at which a human being could alter the outcome. Where no such point exists, or it exists only as a queue nobody works, the decision is made solely by automation and this control applies to it; record alongside each one what it does to the person, because an effect that is legal or comparably significant is what brings the obligation with it. The usual finding is not a disputed judgement call but a decision nobody had noticed was automated at all. Attach the decision inventory with the automated ones marked.

evidenceHint.en: Decision inventory marking each decision that takes effect with no human review, the system producing it, and the effect it has on the person

text.en: List the decisions the organisation makes about an individual.
Record what each system outputs and what is done with it.
Name the person able to change or overturn each outcome.
Mark the decisions no person sees before they take effect.
Note which of those carry a legal or similarly significant effect.

title.en: Deploy the challenge path that hands a contested decision to a named reviewer

description.en: Give an individual subject to a decision made with no person in it a way to object, and carry that objection to someone who can act on it. Three parts have to exist: a control on the notice that carries the decision, a queue the objection lands in, and a reviewer holding written authority to let the outcome stand or replace it. Without the third part the objection reaches somebody who can only restate the result, and the individual has been answered rather than heard. Build the path end to end and prove it by moving one objection through it.

evidenceHint.en: Walk-through of the live path from decision notice to reviewer queue, naming the reviewer and the authority they hold to change the outcome

text.en: Add an objection control to every notice that carries an automated decision.
Point that control at a queue a named reviewer works.
Write down the authority the reviewer holds over the outcome.
Give the reviewer the inputs and the reasoning behind the decision.
Walk one test objection from the notice through to a changed outcome.

title.en: Log each solely automated decision taken in the period and every intervention requested

description.en: Keep a running record of the decisions taken with nobody in the loop: how many of each type, which rule set or model version produced them, who asked for intervention and what the re-taken decision concluded. Record the version explicitly — a decision contested six months later cannot be explained by anyone who does not know what was running when it was made, and the rules will have moved. Attach the automated decision log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Automated decision log for the period: volume per decision type, the rule set or model version in force, and each intervention request with its outcome

text.en: Record the volume of decisions taken automatically by type.
Record the rule set or model version that produced them.
Record every request for human intervention received.
Record the outcome of each decision that was re-taken.
List the decision types that drew no challenge at all.

title.en: Sample the decisions sent for human review and measure how often the outcome changed

description.en: Read the reviewed decisions against what the automation originally produced and count the overturns. An override rate of zero across hundreds of reviews says the review is a signature rather than a decision, and that finding is what this task exists to produce; so is a decision type nobody has ever challenged, which usually means the contest route cannot be reached from where the decision is delivered. Re-check the inventory after each rule or model change, since a change can quietly remove the human step a decision used to pass through. Attach the review-quality analysis for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Review-quality analysis giving the override rate per decision type, the types never challenged, and the inventory re-check following each rule or model change

text.en: Select a sample of decisions sent for human review.
Compare each reviewed outcome against the automated one.
Count how many outcomes the reviewer actually changed.
Read the reasons recorded where nothing was changed.
Re-check the inventory after each rule or model change.

templates.title: Limit processing
templates.description: Implements 7.4.2: the operations performed on PII already held — the jobs, queries, reports and new uses — stay inside what the recorded purposes need, and a use no purpose covers does not run.
templates.objective: To ensure the jobs, queries and reports reading PII already held stay inside the purposes recorded for that PII, so a use no purpose covers never executes.
templates.successCriteria:
Every job, query and report that reads PII appears in the catalogue with the purpose recorded behind it.
Each operation reads only the fields and records its purpose needs, and any left broader carries a stated reason.
A proposed new use of held PII is decided against a recorded purpose before it runs, and refusals are logged with the rest.
Reads that actually executed reconcile to the catalogued purposes, with every divergence closed rather than noted.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the catalogue of PII-reading operations with the purpose behind each and the unaccounted operations flagged.
Collect the change records giving the fields and record scope each operation read before and after narrowing.
Acquire the decision log of proposed new uses of held PII with the outcome of each, refusals included.
Gather the execution logs or query audit trails covering PII reads in the period.
Retrieve the period comparison of executed reads against the catalogued purposes.

Analysis:
Sample scheduled jobs, reports and ad hoc query access from the production estate and check each has a catalogue entry naming a purpose.
Inspect the narrowed operations to confirm the removed fields are absent from the live definition, and weigh the reasons given for those left broad.
Test whether any new use began before its purpose decision was taken, and confirm a refused use left no running job behind it.
Reconcile executed reads against the catalogue and quantify the reads no recorded purpose accounts for.
Follow each recorded divergence through to the change that closed it.

Output:
A catalogue completeness assessment against the PII-reading operations observed running.
A field-scope comparison for narrowed operations with the broad ones still outstanding.
A register of new-use decisions with decision dates set beside first execution.
A list of executed reads with no recorded purpose and the disposition of each.

title.en: Catalogue the jobs, queries and reports that read PII and the purpose each one serves

description.en: Work from the systems inward: list every scheduled job, saved query, report, analytics pipeline and support tool that reads PII, and record against each the purpose from the register that requires the read. The operations nobody can name a purpose for are the deliverable here, not the catalogue itself — they are usually inherited, copied from an older pipeline, or built for a project that has since ended. Attach the catalogue with the purpose against each operation and the unaccounted ones flagged.

evidenceHint.en: Catalogue of PII-reading operations with the purpose recorded behind each and the operations no purpose accounts for flagged

text.en: Enumerate every job, query, report and pipeline that reads PII.
Record the purpose from the register that requires each read.
Note which data categories and which records each one touches.
Flag every operation no recorded purpose accounts for.
Ask each owning team to justify or retire its flagged operations.

title.en: Restrict each operation to the fields and records its purpose actually needs

description.en: Narrow the reads themselves, not the intent behind them: select the columns the purpose requires instead of the whole row, filter each job to the population the purpose covers, and substitute pseudonyms where the work never needs to know which person a row is. Retire the flagged operations no owner would claim. Record what each operation read before and after, and every one left broad with the reason it stays that way. Attach the change record.

evidenceHint.en: Change record giving the fields and record scope each operation read before and after narrowing, with a reason for every one left broad

text.en: Reduce each query to the fields its purpose requires.
Filter every job to the records that purpose covers.
Substitute pseudonyms where identity is not needed.
Turn off the operations no owner would claim.
Record each operation left broad and the reason for it.

title.en: Log every new use proposed for PII already held, with the purpose decision taken before it ran

description.en: Data that exists attracts new uses — a model to train, a report somebody wants, a team that could work faster against the customer table. For each proposal, record what was asked for, which recorded purpose was said to cover it, and the decision taken: proceed, narrow the request, or refuse it until a purpose exists. A refusal is the entry that shows the limit binds, so record refusals as carefully as approvals. Attach the period's decision log.

evidenceHint.en: Decision log of proposed new uses of held PII for the period, each with the purpose relied on and the outcome, refusals included

text.en: Capture each proposed new use of PII already held.
Identify the recorded purpose said to cover it.
Decide whether to proceed, narrow or refuse the request.
Record the decision and the reasoning behind it.
Track the narrowed requests through to what finally ran.

title.en: Compare the reads that actually executed against the purposes recorded for them

description.en: Read the access and query logs for the period and compare what ran against the catalogue: an operation absent from it, a job now reading columns its purpose never needed, a report whose filter was widened, an export nobody remembers approving. Reading the catalogue alone only confirms what was intended. Record every divergence with the operation, what it read beyond its purpose, and how it was resolved. Attach the comparison.

evidenceHint.en: Period comparison of executed PII reads against the catalogued purposes, listing each divergence and how it was resolved

text.en: Extract the period's access and query logs for PII stores.
Match each executed read to a catalogued operation.
List the reads that exceed the purpose recorded for them.
Record how each divergence was resolved or escalated.

templates.title: PII accuracy and quality
templates.description: Implements 7.4.3: every category of PII is held to a stated accuracy and currency standard set by what the purpose using it needs, and records falling short of it are corrected in every store that holds them.
templates.objective: To ensure each category of PII meets the accuracy and currency its purpose demands, and that records falling short are corrected in every store that holds them.
templates.successCriteria:
Each purpose states the attributes that must be correct, the maximum age allowed and the source of truth for the PII it uses.
Entry validation and re-confirmation checks are configured on the fields those standards cover.
A correction reaches every internal store holding the record, not only the system it was entered in.
Sampling live records against the source of truth holds failure rates inside the standard, and each breach carries agreed remediation.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the accuracy requirement table giving, per purpose and PII category, the attributes, the maximum age allowed and the source of truth.
Collect the configuration record of the validation and re-confirmation check applied to each field.
Acquire the list of internal stores a correction is carried through to.
Gather the accuracy correction log showing how each fault surfaced and the value corrected.
Retrieve the accuracy sample test results with the failure rate measured per category.

Analysis:
Check the requirement table covers every purpose in the processing records and that the maximum age set suits how that purpose uses the data.
Exercise the configured validation with sample inputs to confirm the field rejects or flags values outside its standard.
Take corrections from the log and confirm the new value is present in every store named, reporting copies and downstream caches included.
Recalculate the sampled failure rate and set it against the standard stated for that category.
Confirm each breach found in the sample was fed into the correction log and re-tested after the fix, not merely recorded.

Output:
A coverage assessment of accuracy standards against the recorded processing purposes.
Test results for the entry validation and re-confirmation checks, field by field.
A propagation trace for sampled corrections across the internal stores.
A failure-rate summary per PII category with the open remediation listed.

title.en: Determine the accuracy and currency each purpose demands of the PII it uses

description.en: Take each purpose in the register and state what has to be correct about the PII it consumes, how recent that PII must be, and what acting on a wrong value does to the person — a parcel sent to a stale address is a nuisance, an eligibility decision on a stale income is not. The same field answers differently under different purposes, so record it per purpose-and-category pair rather than once per field. Attach the accuracy requirement table with the source of truth named on every row.

evidenceHint.en: Accuracy requirement table giving, per purpose and PII category, the attributes that must be correct, the maximum age allowed and the source of truth each is checked against

text.en: List the purpose and PII category pairs the standard must cover.
State which attributes must be correct for each purpose to work.
Set how recent a value has to be for that purpose to rely on it.
Name the source of truth each attribute is checked against.
Record what acting on a wrong value would do to the person.

title.en: Configure the entry validation and refresh checks that hold each field to its stated standard

description.en: Put the standard into the systems rather than into a document: reject or flag values failing the format and range checks at the point of entry, and schedule a re-confirmation for every attribute the table gives a maximum age. Where a field is copied into a warehouse, cache or service the organisation runs itself, carry the corrected value through to those copies too, or the corrected record and the stale one will both stay in use. Attach the configuration record naming the check applied to each field and the systems it reaches.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration record listing the validation and re-confirmation check applied to each field, and the internal stores a correction is carried through to

text.en: Add format and range checks at every point PII is entered.
Schedule re-confirmation for the attributes given a maximum age.
Route a corrected value into the internal copies of that record.
Record which systems each check was applied in.
Submit a failing value and confirm the check rejects it.

title.en: Log every record found inaccurate or out of date and the correction made to it

description.en: Records fall out of the standard through ordinary life — people move, names change, a source system is re-keyed — so this is a running log rather than an exception report. For each one, record how the fault surfaced (a validation failure, a scheduled refresh, or a mismatch against the source of truth), the value it was corrected to, and the date the correction reached each store holding that record. A correction applied in one system and not the others leaves the organisation acting on both versions at once.

evidenceHint.en: Accuracy correction log for the period, giving the record affected, how the fault surfaced, the value corrected and the stores the correction reached

text.en: Record each inaccurate or stale record as it is found.
Note how the fault came to light in each case.
Enter the corrected value and the date it was applied.
Confirm the correction reached every store holding that record.

title.en: Sample live records against the source of truth and measure how many fail the standard

description.en: Read the data itself rather than the pipeline's success rate: a validation rule nothing ever reached and a refresh job that skipped a table both report no problem. Pull a sample from each category, compare every attribute against the source named in the requirement table, and state the failure rate by category and by purpose. Where a category fails more often than its purpose can tolerate, record what changes as a result — the check, the refresh interval, or that purpose's reliance on the field.

evidenceHint.en: Accuracy sample test reporting the records checked per category, the failure rate measured against the standard and the remediation agreed for each breach

text.en: Draw a sample of live records from each PII category.
Compare each sampled attribute against its source of truth.
Count the records breaching the accuracy or age standard.
State the failure rate by category and by purpose.
Record the change agreed for every category that failed.

templates.title: Transit Protection for PII Held as Controller
templates.description: Implements 7.4.9: PII the organisation processes on its own account is protected on every path it travels, to a standard the organisation sets itself and owes to the individual, including the last leg that reaches them.
templates.objective: To ensure PII the organisation processes on its own account is protected on every path it travels, including the final leg that delivers it to the individual.
templates.successCriteria:
The path inventory covers controller-held PII in transit with purpose, both endpoints and channel, and marks customer-instructed flows out of scope.
Each path carries the protection the organisation determined it owes the PII principal, or an accepted shortfall with the person who accepted it.
Transmissions sent below their path's standard are raised as exceptions and driven to a corrected path.
Probing a path from the recipient's side shows the protection actually negotiated matching the standard set for it.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of paths carrying controller-held PII with purpose, both endpoints and the channel per row.
Collect the per-path protection standard stating the minimum each path must carry and whether it is applied.
Acquire the accepted shortfalls with the name of the person who accepted each.
Gather the exception register of under-protected transmissions with the cause and the date the path was corrected.
Retrieve the path test results giving the protection negotiated at each endpoint probed.

Analysis:
Compare the inventory against egress records and delivery channels to find paths carrying PII that it omits.
Check the out-of-scope markings, confirming the excluded flows are genuinely customer-instructed rather than the organisation's own decisions.
Probe sampled paths as a recipient reaches them and set the negotiated protection beside the standard recorded for that path.
Test the last leg to the individual, covering portal download, email attachment and postal or courier delivery wherever used.
Track exception entries through to the change that corrected the path and measure how long each stayed open.

Output:
An inventory coverage assessment naming PII-carrying paths that were not listed.
A per-path table of required protection against the protection observed in the probe.
A list of accepted shortfalls with the acceptor and the expiry of each acceptance.
Findings on exception closure times and on paths still carrying PII unprotected.

title.en: List the paths carrying PII the organisation processes as controller, and mark the customer-instructed flows out of scope

description.en: Start from the controller half of the records of processing and follow each purpose outward to whatever moves its PII off the system: integrations and APIs, scheduled file transfers, exports and reports, the portal a person logs into, and the email or post by which staff send someone their own data. Flows the organisation runs on a customer's written instruction are marked out of scope here and belong to the processor-side control, because their protection is not the organisation's to decide. Attach the path inventory with the purpose, both endpoints and the channel recorded against every row.

evidenceHint.en: Path inventory of controller-held PII in transit, giving the purpose, both endpoints and the channel per row, with customer-instructed flows marked out of scope

text.en: Take the controller half of the records of processing as the starting list.
Follow each purpose out to the interfaces that move its PII off the system.
Add the channels staff use to send a person their own data.
Mark each flow run on a customer instruction as out of scope here.
Record the two endpoints and the channel against every path.

title.en: Determine the protection each path owes the PII principal, and apply it path by path

description.en: This one is decided on the organisation's own judgement, with nobody to take instruction from. For each path in the inventory, rate what it would mean for the person if the content were read or altered on the way, then set the minimum that path must carry from then on — encryption with authenticated endpoints, no PII in URLs or in the body of ordinary email, a recipient check before a file leaves. Apply it to the paths sitting below their minimum. Where less is knowingly accepted, record the path, the reason and who accepted it; where a path cannot be brought up, the choice open to a controller and to nobody else is to stop sending PII along it, and that decision is recorded here too. Attach the per-path standard with its applied state.

evidenceHint.en: Per-path protection standard showing the minimum each path must carry, whether it is applied, and every accepted shortfall with the person who accepted it

text.en: Rate what a reading of each path in transit would mean for the person.
Set the minimum protection that path must carry from then on.
Apply the setting to every path found below its minimum.
Record each accepted shortfall with its reason and approver.
Decide, for any path that cannot meet it, whether the sending stops.

title.en: Flag each transmission sent with weaker protection than its path requires, and drive each to closure

description.en: Protection settled path by path decays quietly: a certificate lapses, a partner endpoint negotiates down to an older cipher, an overnight job is repointed at a plain endpoint, and PII keeps moving as though nothing changed. Each period this task takes the transport evidence the paths themselves produce and picks out every transmission that travelled with less protection than the path was set to give it. Without that recurring pass the shortfall surfaces from the outside — a recipient's complaint, a partner's audit, a breach notification — months after the PII has already crossed unprotected and long after the traffic can be reconstructed. Catching it while the logs are still fresh bounds the exposure to a known set of transmissions and forces the path itself to be corrected rather than noted.

evidenceHint.en: Period exception register of under-protected PII transmissions, each row naming the path, recipient, date, cause and the date the path was corrected

text.en: Pull the transport logs for every path carrying PII this period.
Compare each transmission with the protection its path applies.
Open an entry for every transmission that fell short.
Name the path, the recipient and the date on each entry.
Give each entry an owner and a date to correct the path.
Close an entry once a later transmission on that path passes.

title.en: Test each path as its recipient sees it and list where PII still crosses unprotected

description.en: Read what the connection actually negotiates rather than what the configuration claims, because a path set correctly a year ago can be answered today by a proxy nobody mentioned. Cover the fallback behaviour — a path that quietly drops to plaintext when the primary route fails is unprotected on exactly the day it matters — and cover the leg that delivers PII to the individual, which is the leg a controller owes and the one most often left out of a scan. Compare what is in use against the inventory and list any path that appeared since without a protection decision behind it. Attach the test with every finding and how it was resolved.

evidenceHint.en: Path test results naming each endpoint probed, the protection actually negotiated, and every unprotected or undecided path found with its resolution

text.en: Probe each endpoint and read the protection actually negotiated.
Force the fallback route and see what it drops to.
Include the leg that delivers PII to the individual.
List any path in use that the inventory does not hold.
Record each finding with the resolution taken.

templates.title: Controller Record of PII Transfers
templates.description: Implements 7.5.3: the organisation keeps its own log of the transfers of PII it decides to make to third parties, so every transfer can be shown afterwards with its date, recipient, contents and the person inside the organisation who authorised it.
templates.objective: To ensure every transfer of PII the organisation itself decides to make can be evidenced afterwards with its date, recipient, contents and internal authoriser.
templates.successCriteria:
The transfers in scope are those the organisation decides on its own account, each with its recipient and deciding function named.
The log specification fixes the fields an entry must carry before the PII reaches its recipient.
Every transfer in the period holds a dated entry giving PII categories, volume, purpose, authorisation and approver.
Outbound export evidence from the systems reconciles to the log with no transfer left unlogged.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scoped list of controller-side transfers with the recipient and the deciding function behind each.
Collect the transfer log specification and the worked example entry completed end to end.
Acquire the dated transfer log for the period.
Gather outbound export evidence from the systems that move PII, such as file transfer records, integration job histories and bulk export audit trails.
Retrieve the authorisation records supporting a sample of logged transfers.

Analysis:
Check each sampled entry carries every field the specification makes mandatory, and identify entries written after the PII had already left.
Reconcile export evidence against the log in both directions: exports with no entry, and entries with no matching export.
Confirm the approver recorded holds authority to release the PII categories and the volume the transfer moved.
Assess whether transfers under a standing arrangement produce an entry per occurrence rather than one entry for the arrangement.
Follow each unlogged transfer found to the explanation recorded and the correction made.

Output:
A completeness test of log entries against the mandatory field specification.
A two-way reconciliation of system export evidence against the transfer log.
An authorisation sample showing the approver and their authority for each transfer tested.
A list of unlogged and late-logged transfers with the resolution of each.

title.en: Identify the transfers of PII to third parties the organisation decides on its own account

description.en: Work through the PII the organisation controls and find every point where some of it goes to another organisation: a partner, a credit reference agency, an insurer, a payroll bureau, a marketing platform, another company in the group. Leave out the movements made on a customer's written instruction, because those are discharged by the customer's own record rather than by this one. What remains is the population this log has to cover, and each entry carries the decision inside the organisation that put the transfer there.

evidenceHint.en: Scoped list of controller-side transfers, naming the recipient, the deciding function and the decision that created each one

text.en: List the third parties that receive PII the organisation controls.
Separate out the sends made on a customer's written instruction.
Record the internal decision that created each remaining transfer.
Name the function that asked for each transfer and still owns it.

title.en: Define the entry a transfer log must carry before PII reaches a recipient

description.en: Settle the fields first: the date the data left, the recipient named as an organisation rather than as a class, the PII categories and the volume, the purpose the transfer serves, the authorisation it rests on, and the named person who approved it. Point the authorisation field at the transfer register that already holds the safeguard, so the log cites the basis instead of re-arguing it. A field set agreed before the first entry is what stops the log decaying into a list of dates nobody can interpret.

evidenceHint.en: Transfer log specification setting the mandatory fields per entry, with one entry completed end to end as a worked example

text.en: Set the fields that every transfer log entry must carry.
Require the recipient to be named as a specific organisation.
Require the name of the person who approved the transfer.
Cite the existing safeguard record rather than restating it.
Complete one entry end to end as the worked example.

title.en: Log each transfer of PII the organisation sends out during the period

description.en: Write the entry when the data moves, not when an auditor asks: a log reconstructed months later records what the paperwork says rather than what happened. Cover the one-off sends as well as the standing feeds, because the spreadsheet emailed to a partner on a Friday is the transfer least likely to be logged and the one a person asking where their data went is most likely to have been in.

evidenceHint.en: Dated transfer log for the period giving recipient, PII categories, volume, purpose, authorisation and approver for every transfer

text.en: Record each standing feed that sent PII during the period.
Record every one-off send, emailed files included.
Enter the date on which the PII actually left.
Name the approver on each entry as it is written.
Close the period by confirming nothing is left unlogged.

title.en: Cross-check the transfer log against the exports that actually left the systems

description.en: Read the outbound evidence on its own terms — integration and API egress logs, file transfer histories, bulk export audit trails, the recipients named on vendor invoices — and look in both directions: an export with no entry behind it, and an entry no system ever performed. The unlogged transfer is the one the organisation cannot explain to the person whose data it carried, so record each discrepancy with an owner and the outcome rather than quietly correcting the log.

evidenceHint.en: Cross-check findings setting outbound export evidence beside the transfer log, listing unlogged transfers and how each was settled

text.en: Pull the outbound export and integration egress logs.
Take the recipient names from vendor invoices and contracts.
Match every outbound export to a transfer log entry.
Match every log entry back to an observed export.
Record each unmatched item with an owner and its outcome.

templates.title: Controller Record of PII Disclosures to Third Parties
templates.description: Implements 7.5.4: every disclosure of PII the organisation itself decides to make is recorded — what was disclosed, to whom, on which ground and who authorised the release — so the person the PII belongs to can later be told which third parties received it.
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation can tell a PII principal which third parties received their PII, by recording every disclosure it decides to make with its ground and authoriser.
templates.successCriteria:
Every route by which the organisation discloses PII on its own decision is inventoried, including the routes that record nothing today.
A disclosure record carries the recipient, the fields released, the ground relied on, the authorising decision and the date sent.
The register can be searched by PII principal, so the third parties that received one person's PII can be listed on request.
Routes that leave no searchable record are named as gaps with remediation, not assumed covered.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the disclosure route inventory naming each channel, the third parties it has reached and the person who decides.
Collect the disclosure record specification with a worked entry completed per route.
Acquire the disclosure register entries covering the period.
Gather the dated recipient-list extract produced for the sampled individual.
Retrieve the gap notes recorded against routes that leave no searchable record.

Analysis:
Walk each inventoried route to confirm a disclosure made through it lands in the register, and look for channels it misses such as support tooling, shared folders and ad hoc email.
Check register entries against the specification for the ground relied on and the authorising decision, treating an unstated ground as a finding.
Rebuild the recipient list for the sampled individual independently and set it against the extract the register produced.
Assess whether the register can be queried by PII principal at all, or only by recipient or date.
Confirm each gap note carries a remediation owner and date rather than standing as an accepted limitation.

Output:
A route inventory assessment naming undocumented disclosure channels.
A test result showing which disclosures name no ground and no authorising decision.
A comparison of the independently rebuilt recipient list against the register extract.
A schedule of routes with no searchable record and the remediation agreed for each.

title.en: Identify every route by which the organisation discloses PII on its own decision

description.en: Go through the ways PII reaches a third party because somebody here decided to hand it over: a police or regulator request, a court order, an insurer or an opposing lawyer asking for a file, a group company asking for an account-holder list, an export a support engineer sends to unblock a partner. What this task is after is the decision-shaped disclosure, the kind that leaves no trace unless a route has been named for it. Record for each route who inside the organisation decides whether the data goes, and mark the routes that disclose today without writing anything down. Attach the route inventory with those unrecorded routes flagged.

evidenceHint.en: Disclosure route inventory naming each channel, the third parties it has reached, the PII categories it can carry, the person who decides, and the routes that record nothing today

text.en: List the channels through which PII leaves the organisation to a named third party.
Name the third parties each channel has actually reached in the last twelve months.
Record the categories of PII each channel is capable of disclosing.
Name the person here who decides whether a disclosure on that route goes ahead.
Mark every route that discloses today without leaving a record behind.

title.en: Define the fields a disclosure record must carry to answer the individual it concerns

description.en: Fix what an entry must contain before it counts as recorded, and test each field against the question the person whose PII it was is entitled to put months later: who was given my data, what of it, and on what basis. That means the recipient named as an organisation and a contact rather than as 'law enforcement', the PII listed field by field rather than as 'account details', the ground the organisation relied on when it decided to disclose, and the name of whoever authorised the release. Fill one worked entry per route so the fields are proved against a real disclosure instead of agreed in the abstract. Attach the record specification with its worked entries.

evidenceHint.en: Disclosure record specification listing the mandatory fields, with one worked entry completed per disclosure route

text.en: Set the fields every disclosure entry must carry before it can be closed.
Require the recipient to be named as an organisation and a contact.
Require the PII released to be listed by category and by field.
Record the ground the organisation relied on when it decided to disclose.
Name the person here who authorised the release of the data.
Complete one worked entry per route to prove the fields hold up.

title.en: File a record of what went to which third party, one entry per disclosure

description.en: Every time the organisation decides on its own account to hand PII to an outside party, one entry goes into the disclosure register while the release is still fresh. Reconstructed months later a disclosure becomes a guess: the recipient is half-remembered, the exact fields are not, and nobody can say who approved it. That guess is what an individual gets when they ask who now holds their data, and what a regulator gets when it asks the organisation to account for a release it made. Filing at the moment of release keeps the register an account of what happened rather than a reconstruction of what probably happened.

evidenceHint.en: Disclosure register entries covering the period, each carrying recipient, fields released, authorising decision and date sent

text.en: Open a disclosure entry as soon as the release is authorised.
Name the receiving organisation and the contact who took delivery.
Write down which PII fields left and the purpose the recipient has for them.
Attach the authorisation and the name of whoever gave it.
Stamp the entry with the date and the channel the PII travelled by.

title.en: Trace one individual through the disclosure log and rebuild the recipient list they are owed

description.en: A disclosure log can look complete and still fail the one question it exists to answer: a person asks who the organisation handed their PII to, and nobody can produce the list. Take an individual who was actually disclosed during the period, search the log for them, and write out the recipients it gives back. Then hold that answer against the disclosure routes named in the scope inventory, because a route that moves PII but leaves no searchable record is exactly the failure this task looks for. Attach the returned recipient list and every gap it exposed.

evidenceHint.en: Dated recipient-list extract for the sampled individual, held against the disclosure routes, with a gap note for every route that left no searchable record

text.en: Pick one individual whose PII was disclosed to a third party during the period.
Search the disclosure log for every record that names that individual.
Write out the recipient list the search returns, one row per recipient and date.
Hold that list against the disclosure routes named in the scope inventory.
Raise a gap for any route that moved the individual's PII without leaving a record.

templates.title: Customer Processing Agreement
templates.description: Implements 8.2.1: every engagement where the organisation processes PII for a customer is covered by a written agreement that fixes which party is controller and which is processor, and states the processing obligations owed.
templates.objective: To ensure every engagement in which the organisation processes PII for a customer runs under written terms fixing the controller and processor roles and the obligations owed.
templates.successCriteria:
Each engagement sits in the customer processing register with the service supplied, the PII categories involved and the agreement governing it.
The approved terms state which party is controller and which is processor, and fix instructed processing, PII categories, duration and the instruction channel.
Signings, amendments and supersessions are logged with effective dates and the executed copy indexed against each.
No customer sends PII without executed terms in force at the time that processing happens.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the customer processing register with one row per engagement and the governing agreement or the recorded gap.
Collect the approved processing terms and the clause map locating roles, instructed processing, PII categories, duration and the instruction channel.
Acquire the customer agreement log of signings, amendments and supersessions with their effective dates.
Gather executed copies for a sample of engagements.
Retrieve the agreement coverage verification listing uncovered customers and superseded versions.

Analysis:
Reconcile the register against customer and billing records to find engagements handling PII that it omits.
Read the sampled executed copies against the clause map and confirm each mapped clause is present in the version actually signed, not only in the template.
Test the role allocation against how the engagement operates, since terms naming the organisation controller while it acts only on instruction are a finding.
Compare each agreement's effective date against the date PII first flowed for that customer.
Confirm superseded versions were withdrawn rather than left running alongside the current terms.

Output:
A register completeness assessment against the live customer base.
A clause-presence test result for the sampled executed agreements.
A timeline comparison of effective dates against first processing of customer PII.
A list of uncovered customers and stale term versions with the date each was papered.

title.en: List each engagement where the organisation processes PII for a customer and the agreement governing it

description.en: Work from what actually brings customer data in - the tenant list, onboarding records and billing - and write one row per engagement giving the service supplied, the categories of PII it involves and the signed document that governs the processing. Where the only paper is a service contract carrying no processing terms, or none can be found, record that as a gap rather than leaving the cell empty: an unpapered engagement is the reason the register exists. Attach the register dated at the point it was compiled.

evidenceHint.en: Customer processing register: one row per engagement giving the service supplied, the PII categories involved and the governing agreement or the recorded gap

text.en: Pull the customer list from tenant, onboarding and billing records.
Record the service supplied under each customer engagement.
Name the PII categories that engagement involves.
Cite the signed document governing each engagement.
Mark every engagement carrying no processing terms as a gap.

title.en: Write the processing terms that state which party is controller and which is processor

description.en: Draft the terms the organisation offers as processor so a reader can tell, without asking anyone, who is controller and who is processor for each activity, what the organisation is instructed to do, which categories of PII and of people are involved, how long the processing runs, and where the customer's documented instructions are given and amended. Terms that describe the service but never allocate the roles leave the obligation unassigned, which is the failure this control exists to prevent. Attach the approved terms with the clause carrying each element marked.

evidenceHint.en: Approved processing terms with a clause map showing where roles, instructed processing, PII categories, duration and the instruction channel are each stated

text.en: State which party is controller and which is processor.
Describe the processing the organisation is instructed to perform.
List the PII categories and the people that data concerns.
Set how long the agreed processing runs for.
Name the channel where documented instructions are given.
Have the drafted terms approved before they are offered.

title.en: Log every customer agreement signed, amended or superseded with the date it took effect

description.en: Coverage lapses in contract administration rather than in drafting, so keep one running record: each agreement executed, each amendment, each set of terms replaced by a later version, with the customer, the effective date and the version now in force. Record the date PII first reached the service beside the date the agreement took effect, because the order of those two dates is what this control asks about. Attach the period's log with the executed copies indexed against it.

evidenceHint.en: Customer agreement log for the period: signings, amendments and supersessions with effective dates, the version in force and the executed copy indexed against each

text.en: Record each customer agreement executed in the period.
Note the effective date and the version now in force.
Record when PII first reached the service for that customer.
Index the executed copy against its log entry.
Log each amendment and the terms version it replaced.

title.en: Verify that every customer sending PII is covered by executed terms in force

description.en: Read the two sides against each other: the tenants and integrations that actually sent personal data in during the period, and the agreement log. Both directions are findings - a customer whose data is being processed under no executed terms, and an executed agreement left on terms the organisation has since replaced, so the version in force is not the version it operates to. Take the active side from system evidence rather than the sales list, which lags. Record each discrepancy with its correction. Attach the verification with its findings.

evidenceHint.en: Agreement coverage verification listing uncovered customers and superseded term versions, each with its correction and the date it was papered

text.en: Extract the tenants that sent PII during the period.
Compare that list against the customer agreement log.
Flag any customer processed without executed terms.
Flag agreements left on a superseded version of the terms.
Record the correction and the date each gap was closed.

templates.title: Own-purpose use of customer PII
templates.description: Implements 8.2.2: customer PII is processed only for the purposes the customer has instructed, and every internal use that serves the organisation's own ends is either stopped or brought under a recorded instruction.
templates.objective: To ensure customer PII serves only the purposes the customer instructed, so an internal use of it that no instruction covers is stopped or brought under a recorded one.
templates.successCriteria:
Every internal system and team reading customer PII is inventoried with the customer instruction relied on, and uncovered uses are marked as such.
Each uncovered use has stopped or gained an instruction, with its copies and derived artefacts purged on a recorded date.
A proposal to use customer PII for an internal purpose is decided and logged before that use begins.
Observed outbound flows of customer PII reconcile to instructions that permit them.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of internal uses of customer PII with the receiving system, the reading team and the instruction relied on.
Collect the change record for each uncovered use stating whether it stopped or gained an instruction.
Acquire the purge records for copies and derived artefacts such as analytics extracts, model training sets and reporting warehouses.
Gather the decision log of internal requests to use customer PII with the answer given to each.
Retrieve the period reconciliation of observed outbound flows against the recorded instructions.

Analysis:
Sample internal analytics, product and support systems for customer PII and check each against the inventory and the instruction cited for it.
Test whether the instruction relied on authorises the use claimed, rather than a neighbouring purpose in the same agreement.
Confirm the purges reached derived artefacts as well as the primary copy, since a deleted source with a surviving training set leaves the use running.
Compare each decision date in the log against the date that use first read customer PII.
Trace flows found with no instruction behind them to the action taken on them.

Output:
An inventory assessment against the systems observed holding customer PII.
An instruction-to-use mapping showing which uses the cited instruction genuinely covers.
Purge confirmation for copies and derived artefacts with the date of each.
A list of internal uses begun before their decision, and flows still lacking an instruction.

title.en: Trace every internal use of customer PII that serves the organisation's own ends

description.en: Customer PII arrives to be processed for the customer, then quietly acquires second readers: a product analytics pipeline, a model-training corpus, a benchmark the organisation publishes, a demo environment seeded from production, an engineer reproducing a bug against live records. Follow the data out of the service boundary and record every internal destination it reaches, the team that reads it there, and the purpose they read it for. Against each use, name the customer instruction it is claimed to rest on — and mark the ones resting on nothing, because that mark is the deliverable rather than the inventory around it.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of internal uses of customer PII, giving each receiving system, the team reading it, and the customer instruction relied on, with the uncovered uses marked

text.en: Follow customer PII out of the production service into every internal system that receives a copy.
Record the team reading each copy and the purpose they read it for.
Cite the customer instruction that is claimed to permit each use.
Mark every internal use that no instruction covers.
Circulate the marked list to the owners of those systems.

title.en: Separate customer PII from the internal systems whose use no instruction covers

description.en: Take the marked uses one at a time. Either the customer instruction is obtained and written down, or the feed stops and the copies already sitting in that system are removed. The derived artefacts are the half that gets forgotten: a trained model, an aggregate table and a cached export all outlive the pipeline that fed them, and a stopped feed with the derivatives left in place has changed nothing about what the organisation still holds for its own benefit. Record for each marked use which way it went, on what date, and exactly what was purged.

evidenceHint.en: Change record per uncovered use stating whether it stopped or gained an instruction, listing the copies and derived artefacts purged and the date

text.en: Decide for each marked use whether an instruction will be obtained or the use stops.
Disconnect the feed for every use that is stopping.
Purge the copies already held in those internal systems.
Delete or retrain the artefacts derived from that data.
Record the outcome, date and what was purged for each use.

title.en: Register each proposal to use customer PII for an internal purpose and record the decision

description.en: New own-purpose uses arrive as ordinary requests — a data-science team asking for a production extract, a marketing team asking for usage figures by named customer, a support tool wanting live records to reproduce a fault. Put them through one intake and record, for each, the internal purpose asked for, the customer instruction it was checked against, and the answer given. A refusal is as much the evidence as an approval: a log containing only approvals is a log of a check nobody applied.

evidenceHint.en: Decision log of internal requests to use customer PII, each entry giving the purpose asked for, the instruction checked, and the answer given

text.en: Route every internal request for customer PII into a single intake.
Record the internal purpose the requester is asking for.
Check the request against the customer instruction that would permit it.
Record the decision and the reason it was given.
Report the period's approvals and refusals to the privacy owner.

title.en: Reconcile the outbound flows of customer PII against the instructions that permit them

description.en: Between reviews an integration is added, a warehouse job widens its query, a vendor is wired into the support tool. Take the flows actually leaving the customer-service boundary — read from egress records, warehouse job definitions and the integrations in place — and set them beside the instructions recorded above. List every flow no instruction accounts for, and treat the length of that list, not the fact the review happened, as the result of this task.

evidenceHint.en: Period reconciliation of observed outbound PII flows against the recorded customer instructions, listing every flow with no instruction behind it

text.en: Collect the flows actually leaving the service boundary this period.
Compare each against the recorded customer instructions.
List every flow that no instruction accounts for.
Raise each unexplained flow with the owning team for correction.
Record the count of unexplained flows beside the previous period's.

templates.title: Infringing customer instructions
templates.description: Implements 8.2.4: an instruction from a controller customer that appears to breach applicable privacy law is recognised by the staff who receive it, assessed, and put back to that customer in writing rather than quietly carried out.
templates.objective: To ensure an instruction from a controller customer that appears to breach privacy law is recognised on arrival, assessed, and put back to that customer in writing before it is worked.
templates.successCriteria:
Every route by which customer instructions arrive is inventoried with the role that first reads one.
A published trigger list tells those readers which instruction patterns must be raised, and names one assessor and one raising route.
An instruction assessed as potentially infringing is notified to the customer in writing, and the reply is kept with it.
Sampling the instructions received finds none that met a trigger and was never raised.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of customer-instruction intake routes naming the role that first receives each and where it goes next.
Collect the published trigger list of instruction patterns that must be raised, with the named assessor and the single raising route.
Acquire the file of written infringement notices sent in the period with the customer's reply to each.
Gather the sample review of instructions received and the misses it identified.
Retrieve the briefing or training records showing the trigger list reached the receiving roles.

Analysis:
Check the intake inventory against how instructions actually arrive, including support tickets, account-manager email and in-product requests.
Assess whether each trigger is stated concretely enough for a first reader to apply without legal judgement.
Read sampled instructions against the trigger list and identify any that met a trigger but produced no assessment.
Confirm the written notice preceded the work, and read the replies for instructions the customer pressed regardless.
Ask staff on the intake routes to name the raising route and compare the answers against the published one.

Output:
An intake assessment naming instruction channels nobody is watching.
A trigger applicability review flagging wording too vague for a first reader to act on.
A sample result setting instructions raised against instructions that met a trigger.
A list of notices sent after the instruction was already worked, with the outcome of each.

title.en: Identify the points where customer instructions arrive and who first reads them

description.en: An instruction rarely arrives labelled as one. It comes as a support ticket, a migration request to an engineer, a configuration change made in the product, a line in an account manager's email. Work out every route by which a customer can tell this organisation to do something with their PII, and record for each route the role that receives it first — that person is the only one positioned to notice a problem before the work is done. Attach the route inventory with the receiving role named against each.

evidenceHint.en: Inventory of customer-instruction intake routes, naming the role that first receives each and where it goes next

text.en: List each channel through which a customer sends processing instructions.
Name the role that first reads an instruction on each channel.
Record where an instruction can reach an engineer with no review at all.
Note which channels keep a durable written record of the instruction.

title.en: Define the tests that make an instruction reportable and the route for raising one

description.en: Support staff and engineers are not lawyers, so the recognition has to be reduced to a short list of readable signals: an instruction to use PII for something the customer's own notice does not cover, to hold it past the period the customer set, to release it to a party the customer cannot name, to restore data the customer previously asked to be erased. Pair the list with one route for raising a concern and the person who rules on it, so the question does not die in the thread it was asked in. Attach the trigger list and the raising route as published to staff.

evidenceHint.en: Published trigger list of instruction patterns that must be raised, with the named assessor and the single raising route

text.en: Write the signals that mark an instruction as questionable.
Name the assessor who rules on a raised instruction.
Record whether processing pauses while an assessment runs.
Publish the route to staff on every intake channel identified.

title.en: Notify the customer in writing when an instruction is assessed as potentially infringing

description.en: Where the assessment concludes the instruction may breach applicable privacy law, say so to the customer in writing: identify the instruction, the date it was received, what about it appears unlawful, and what this organisation is doing with it in the meantime. A concern voiced to an account manager on a call leaves nothing behind, and it is the written notice — with whatever the customer answers — that shows the obligation was met. Attach the notices issued in the period together with the customer replies.

evidenceHint.en: File of written infringement notices sent to customers in the period, each with the instruction it concerns and the customer's reply

text.en: Record the instruction and the date it was received.
State plainly which requirement the instruction appears to breach.
Send the notice to the customer contact named in the agreement.
Store the notice and any customer reply with the case record.

title.en: Sample the instructions received in the period and check the questionable ones were raised

description.en: The failure mode here is silence: a control that only produces evidence when somebody speaks up looks perfect during a period in which nobody spoke up. Take a sample of instructions actually received across the routes inventoried, apply the trigger list to each independently, and list any that met a trigger yet were never raised, with why they were missed. A period with no notices at all is something to explain — either nothing questionable arrived, or nothing questionable was noticed.

evidenceHint.en: Sample review of instructions received, listing every instruction that met a trigger but was never raised and the cause of each miss

text.en: Pull a sample of instructions from each intake route.
Apply the trigger list to every instruction in the sample.
List instructions that met a trigger but were never raised.
Explain a period that produced no notices at all.

templates.title: Processor Assistance with PII-Principal Requests
templates.description: Implements 8.3.1: the service gives each controller customer the means to answer a PII-principal request about the PII it holds on their behalf — the functions to export, correct and erase it, worked only on the customer's written instruction, with the output handed back so the customer can make the response they owe the individual.
templates.objective: To ensure each controller customer can answer a PII-principal request against the PII the service holds for them, worked only on that customer's written instruction.
templates.successCriteria:
The capability statement names, per request type, what the service performs for the customer and what remains the customer's to do.
The export, correction and erasure functions reach every customer data store the statement claims and return a completion record.
Each instruction worked records the authorisation check made, the systems acted in and the output handed back.
A principal approaching the service directly is forwarded to the customer unanswered, and turnarounds close inside the customer's own deadline.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the per-request-type capability statement naming the actions the service performs and the customer stores each reaches.
Collect the customer-facing service documentation for the export, correction, erasure and completion-record calls.
Acquire the assistance log with instruction, authorisation check, systems acted in and output returned.
Gather the record of principal approaches received directly and forwarded on unanswered.
Retrieve the turnaround analysis setting each closed instruction against the customer's own response deadline.

Analysis:
Exercise the export and erasure calls in a test tenant and compare what they return against the customer stores listed, backups, logs and sub-processor holdings included.
Verify the authorisation check on sampled instructions, confirming each came from an authorised customer contact rather than from the principal.
Confirm forwarded approaches were passed on without the service answering the principal on the customer's behalf.
Measure turnaround against the customer's deadline and attribute each overrun to the service or to a sub-processor.
Check that instructions the service could only part-complete were reported back rather than closed as done.

Output:
A capability-to-store coverage map naming customer stores no function reaches.
Test results for the export, correction and erasure calls exercised in the test tenant.
An authorisation sample recording the contact verified for each instruction worked.
A turnaround table naming overruns, sub-processor delays and part-completed instructions.

title.en: Determine which part of each rights request the service can discharge for the customer

description.en: A customer cannot answer an individual unless they know what the service will do for them and what is left on their own side. Take each request type a controller customer may pass down — access, a copy, correction, erasure, restriction — and record what the service can perform against the PII it holds for them, which of their data stores that reaches, and what the customer still has to do in systems the service never sees. Request types the service cannot act on at all belong on the same statement: an unstated gap is discovered by the customer on the day a deadline is running, not before.

evidenceHint.en: Per-request-type capability statement naming the actions the service performs for the customer, the customer data stores each action reaches, and the actions left with the customer

text.en: List the rights request types customers ask the service to act on.
Record which customer data stores each of those actions must reach.
Name the actions that remain the customer's own to perform.
Mark the request types the service cannot act on at all.

title.en: Build the export, correction and erasure functions the customer drives against their own PII
